newsitem.title: FRANCE: French economists see Bund/OAT spread at zero.
newsitem.headline: French economists see Bund/OAT spread at zero.

text.p: The spread between French government bonds (OATs) and equivalent German Bunds is expected to return to zero this year from around minus eight basis points now, a panel of economists from banks and industry said on Wednesday.

The French Association of Company Treasurers (Afede) said it saw 10-year rates in France and Germany reaching 6.2 percent between now and June 1997 and 6.3 percent between now and the end of the year.
French 10-year bonds are currently yielding around 5.86 percent, eight basis points below German 10-year yields.
Afede said in a statement that an expected rise in U.S. long-term rates would partly affect European long-term rates.
It said it saw very little change in European short-term rates, since it did not expect a new weakening in the dollar.
It forecast that the franc would be at 3.38 per mark this year, compared with its current level of 3.3770.
